title.en: Akshi and Toshi on the track

text.en: Akshi runs 5 rounds on a rectangular outer track and Toshi runs 7 rounds on the inner track. Who ran farther? To answer, we need the distance around each track, which is its perimeter. Later, to cover a floor with tiles or plan a garden, we need the space inside a shape, which is its area. This chapter shows how perimeter and area are measured, how they are different, and how a rectangle helps us find the area of a triangle.

The perimeter of a closed plane figure is the distance covered along its boundary when we go around it once. For a polygon it is the sum of the lengths of all its sides. A rectangle has equal opposite sides, so its perimeter is length + breadth + length + breadth, which equals 2 x (length + breadth). For a rectangle 12 cm by 8 cm it is 2 x (12 + 8) = 40 cm. A square has four equal sides, so its perimeter is 4 times the side. Debojeet needs 4 m of coloured tape for a square frame of side 1 m. For a triangle, add the three sides. If the perimeter is 55 cm and two sides are 20 cm and 14 cm, the third side is 55 - 20 - 14 = 21 cm. A regular polygon has all sides equal, so its perimeter is the number of sides times the length of one side. A string of 36 cm can make a square of side 9 cm, an equilateral triangle of side 12 cm, or a regular hexagon of side 6 cm.
Akshi track is a rectangle of 70 m by 40 m, so one round is 2 x (70 + 40) = 220 m, and 5 rounds are 1100 m. Toshi inner track gives 180 m a round, so 7 rounds are 1260 m. Toshi ran farther even though Akshi has the longer track. To fence a rectangular park 150 m by 120 m, the perimeter is 2 x (150 + 120) = 540 m. At Rs 40 a metre the fence costs 540 x 40 = Rs 21,600. When the perimeter is known we can find a missing side. A rectangle of perimeter 14 cm and breadth 2 cm has length 14 / 2 - 2 = 5 cm, and a square of perimeter 20 cm has side 5 cm. In races on square tracks the finishing line is common, so runners on the outer track start ahead. This is why the starting points of different lanes are staggered.
Area is the amount of surface inside a closed figure. We measure it by counting unit squares that cover the figure without gaps or overlaps. A unit square of side 1 cm has an area of 1 sq cm. The area of a rectangle is length x breadth. For a garden 25 m long with an area of 300 sq m, the width is 300 / 25 = 12 m. The area of a square is side x side. Square units are used for area, such as sq cm, sq m and sq km, and plain units like cm and m are used for perimeter. Using area we can find costs and counts. Tiling a rectangle 500 m by 200 m at Rs 8 for each 100 sq m costs 100,000 / 100 x 8 = Rs 8000. A grove 100 m by 50 m has 5000 sq m, so at 25 sq m a tree it holds 200 trees.
Many shapes are not rectangles, but we can cut them into rectangles, find each area and add. An L shaped figure is split into two rectangles in this way. We can also subtract. A floor of 5 m by 4 m has an area of 20 sq m, and a 3 m square carpet covers 9 sq m, so 11 sq m is not carpeted. A garden of 15 m by 12 m has area 180 sq m, and four beds of 2 m by 1 m take 8 sq m, leaving 172 sq m for the lawn. Charan house plan is a rectangular plot divided into rooms. The area of the whole plot is the sum of the areas of the rooms, and the missing sides are found from the known sides.
Draw a rectangle and cut along a diagonal. The two triangles fit exactly on each other, so each is half of the rectangle. The area of a right triangle is half of the area of the rectangle on its two shorter sides. For any triangle ABE standing on the side AB of a rectangle ABCD whose top vertex E is on side CD, drop the perpendicular EF. The triangle splits into two right triangles, each half of a smaller rectangle, so the whole triangle is half of rectangle ABCD. We can therefore find the area of a triangle on grid paper by building a rectangle around it and taking half. More shapes can be handled by splitting them into rectangles and triangles.
Shapes with the same area need not have the same perimeter. With 9 unit squares joined edge to edge, a 3 by 3 square has the smallest perimeter, 12 units, and a long strip of 9 by 1 has the largest, 20 units. A perimeter of 18 units can be made with several different shapes, so perimeter alone does not decide the shape. A new unit square brings four edges, but each whole side it shares removes two counted edges. One shared side adds two units to the perimeter, two shared sides leave it unchanged, and three shared sides take away two units. Touching at a corner hides no edge. When a square paper is cut along the fold into two rectangles, the two perimeters together are 1.5 times the square perimeter, but the total area stays the same.

Imagine two rectangles made of one-centimetre tiles. One has five columns of two tiles and the other has ten columns of one tile. Predict whether they need the same length of border tape.
Both rectangles cover ten square centimetres. But going around the first takes fourteen centimetres, while going around the thin strip takes twenty-two centimetres.
For another check, join three unit squares in a straight row. Start with twelve edges, then remove two counted edges for each of the two joins. The outside has eight unit edges.

Make a two-by-two square with its top-right tile missing. That L shape also has three tiles and eight outside edges. Filling the gap gives it four square units of area, and its perimeter stays at eight.

An L-shaped floor fits inside an eight-metre by six-metre rectangle with a three-metre by two-metre corner missing. Start with forty-eight square metres and subtract the six square metres outside the floor.
The floor covers forty-two square metres. Check by splitting it into a strip eight metres by four metres and a strip five metres by two metres. Their areas add to the same total.
For a triangle with an eight-centimetre base and a perpendicular height of five centimetres, imagine the matching rectangle. It covers forty square centimetres, so the triangle takes half that area.
The height is the shortest distance from the opposite vertex to the base line. Follow the line that meets the base at a right angle instead of using a sloping side.

board.text: Height is perpendicular to the base

problem.en: A rectangular park is 150 m long and 120 m wide. Find the cost of fencing it at Rs 40 a metre, and the area of the park.

why.en: Fencing goes around, so use the perimeter.
Multiply the length by the rate per metre.
Area is length times breadth, in square units.

problem.en: A wire is bent into a rectangle 5 cm by 3 cm. It is then straightened and bent into a square. Find the side of the square.

text.en: Length of wire = perimeter = 2 x (5 + 3) = 16 cm.

why.en: The wire length equals the perimeter.

text.en: A square has 4 equal sides, so each side = 16 / 4.
Side = 4 cm.

why.en: The wire length is the same, so the perimeter is unchanged.

problem.en: A floor 5 m long and 4 m wide has a square carpet of side 3 m laid on it. How much floor is not carpeted?

text.en: Floor area = 5 x 4 = 20 sq m.
Carpet area = 3 x 3 = 9 sq m.
Uncovered area = 20 - 9 = 11 sq m.

why.en: Subtract the part that is covered.

problem.en: A rectangle is 12 cm by 8 cm. A diagonal cuts it into two triangles. Find the area of each triangle.

text.en: Area of rectangle = 12 x 8 = 96 sq cm.

why.en: Find the area of the whole rectangle first.

text.en: The diagonal makes two triangles that fit exactly on each other.
Area of each triangle = 96 / 2 = 48 sq cm.

why.en: Each triangle is half the rectangle.

prompt.en: Explain the difference between perimeter and area, and how you can find the area of a triangle.

requiredIdeas.en: Perimeter is the distance around a shape; area is the surface inside.
Perimeter uses units like cm and m; area uses square units like sq cm and sq m.
A rectangle has area length x breadth and perimeter 2 x (length + breadth).
A triangle on a rectangle uses half the rectangle area.

commonMisconceptions.en: Using the perimeter formula to find the area, or the other way round.
Writing area in plain cm instead of sq cm.
Thinking that bigger area always means bigger perimeter.
Forgetting to halve when finding the area of a triangle from a rectangle.

points.en: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary: for a rectangle 2 x (length + breadth), for a square 4 x side.
Area is the surface inside a figure, measured in square units; a rectangle has area length x breadth.
Complex shapes are cut into rectangles and the areas are added or subtracted.
A diagonal cuts a rectangle into two triangles of equal area, so a right triangle has half the area of the rectangle.
Two shapes can have the same area but different perimeters.
Use perimeter for fencing and borders, and area for tiling, painting and covering.
